newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crude trades steady, Brent deals rumoured.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crude trades steady, Brent deals rumoured.

text.p: North Sea crude oil markets traded at steady levels on Wednesday with healthy activity in the non-Brent grades and rumours of several private benchmark blend deals, traders said.
But paper markets were lifeless, with numbers sticking at softish levels, and very little business done.
Crude differentials remained static, though one trader called prices "a bit toppy." Others saw the market balanced, with attention shifting already to third decade July cargoes.

Three Statfjord cargoes were heard traded, with one confirmed done at dated Brent +30 cents. There was no price reaction to the production problems that have pushed all 30 of the July Statfjord loading dates back by 48 hours.
Ekofisk, Gullfaks A and Beryl cargoes all went for values similar to last traded numbers, and a Draugen went for an undisclosed amount.
The major holding much of this month's Brent production refused to confirm or deny his involvement in the two cargo deals rumoured done on a private and confidential basis.
Much of the day was overshadowed by the OPEC oil ministers meeting in Vienna and Iraq's declaration that it intended to restart crude exports within seven to 10 days if it could.

There was considerable market scepticism that that target could be achieved, given the considerable political and logistic obstacles still to be overcome, but Baghdad's willingness to ship oil at least reduced market tension over future supplies.
News that Saudi Arabia and Iran were pressuring Venezuela and other OPEC quota busters to restrain production and help support sagging oil prices were also being discounted.
